dimensions.assessment: Affects state and local law enforcement agencies applying for Byrne JAG grants, individuals convicted of felony animal cruelty, and the public accessing the new database.
dimensions.evidence: applicant will report to the Attorney General data on felony convictions under State law that involved cruelty to animals including the name of any individual convicted

dimensions.assessment: Imposes new reporting burdens on state and local governments for grant eligibility and creates a public federal registry of animal cruelty felony convictions.
dimensions.evidence: establish a publicly accessible database containing the data reported

dimensions.assessment: Directs the Department of Justice to establish and maintain a database, but does not authorize new funding appropriations for grants.
dimensions.evidence: establish a publicly accessible database containing the data reported

dimensions.assessment: Amends the Omnibus Crime Control and Safe Streets Act of 1968 to add grant certification requirements and mandate a new DOJ database.
dimensions.evidence: The Omnibus Crime Control and Safe Streets Act ... is amended

dimensions.assessment: Permanent reporting requirement for grant applicants starting in the first fiscal year beginning two years after enactment.
dimensions.evidence: apply to applications for grants submitted during the first fiscal year that begins after the date that is 2 years after the date of enactment

missing_information: Estimated administrative cost for the Department of Justice to build and maintain the public database.
importance_detail.rationale: Conditions Byrne Justice Assistance Grants on states reporting felony animal cruelty convictions and names of convicted individuals, and mandates that the DOJ establish a publicly accessible database for this data.
